en.greeting: Hi! Today you'll add more verbs to your -ing list and your to list, and learn to use -ing as a subject and after words like in and at. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: More verbs + -ing
steps.text: You know I want to go and I enjoy swimming. Now let's grow the -ing list.
steps.body: Recap: **want, need, hope + to** (I want **to go**); **enjoy, finish, don't mind + -ing** (I enjoy **swimming**). Eight more verbs take **-ing**: **avoid, suggest, consider, keep, mind, practise, miss, can't stand**. There's no rule you can see: learn each verb with its partner, like a new word. Trap: *menyarankan **untuk** pergi* makes people say `suggested to go`, but suggest takes -ing: She suggested **going** by train.

steps.title: -ing verbs in real life
steps.text: Look at the -ing after each verb.
steps.body: **practise** is the British spelling; American English writes **practice** for the verb too. **mind** is mostly in questions and negatives: *Would you mind waiting?* / *I don't mind walking.*

examples.en: I avoid driving in Jakarta at rush hour.
examples.id: Saya menghindari menyetir di Jakarta saat jam sibuk.

examples.en: Pak Hasan suggested meeting at the café near the office.
examples.id: Pak Hasan menyarankan bertemu di kafe dekat kantor.

examples.en: Rina is considering taking a part-time job.
examples.id: Rina sedang mempertimbangkan untuk mengambil kerja paruh waktu.

examples.en: My phone keeps turning off.
examples.id: HP saya mati terus.

examples.en: I miss eating my mother's rendang.
examples.id: Saya kangen makan rendang buatan ibu saya.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: A colleague asks how to get to Bandung. What do you suggest?

question.prompt: Complete: I suggest ___ the train. It's faster than the bus.
question.explanation: suggest is followed by **-ing**: I suggest **taking** the train. `suggest to take` comes from Indonesian *menyarankan untuk*, and `suggest take` has no -ing.

steps.title: More verbs + to
steps.text: Now the other list: verbs that take to + base form.
steps.body: Like *want* and *hope*, these verbs take **to + base form** (the plain verb: *go, buy*): **decide, plan, afford, agree, refuse, promise, manage, offer, expect**. **afford** (mampu membayar) almost always comes with **can / can't**: We can't afford **to buy** a car, not `can't afford buying`. **manage to** = *berhasil* (it was hard, but you did it), not *mengatur*. **offer to** = *menawarkan diri*.

steps.title: to verbs in real life
steps.text: Here they are in sentences. Look for to + base form.

examples.en: Sari decided to look for a new job.
examples.id: Sari memutuskan untuk mencari pekerjaan baru.

examples.en: Many young people can't afford to buy a house in Jakarta.
examples.id: Banyak anak muda tidak mampu membeli rumah di Jakarta.

examples.en: The shop refused to give me a refund.
examples.id: Toko itu menolak mengembalikan uang saya.

examples.en: The traffic was terrible, but we managed to catch the train.
examples.id: Macetnya parah, tapi kami berhasil naik kereta itu.

examples.en: Dimas offered to drive me to the airport.
examples.id: Dimas menawarkan diri untuk mengantar saya ke bandara.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Rents are high. Say that you don't have enough money for a big house.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Kami tidak mampu menyewa rumah besar.
question.solution: We can't afford to rent a big house.
question.explanation: **afford** takes **to + base form**: can't afford **to rent**. *tidak mampu* = can't afford; *menyewa* = rent.

steps.title: -ing as a subject and after prepositions
steps.text: Last part: two more places where English needs -ing.
steps.body: **1. As the subject** (what the sentence is about): **Swimming** is good for you. Indonesian *Berenang baik untuk kesehatan* keeps the plain verb, so people write `Swim is good`. The verb after it is singular: Swimming **is**. **2. After a preposition**, a small linking word like *in, at, of, for, before, after, without, instead of*: use a noun or **-ing**, never the base form: interested **in learning**, not `interested in learn`.

steps.title: -ing at work
steps.text: Here are -ing subjects and -ing after prepositions.
steps.body: A phrase to remember: **I look forward to meeting you.** Here *to* is a preposition (like *to the bank*), so -ing follows.

examples.en: Taking the KRL is cheaper than taking a taxi.
examples.id: Naik KRL lebih murah daripada naik taksi.

examples.en: Reading the news every morning helps me at work.
examples.id: Membaca berita setiap pagi membantu saya di kantor.

examples.en: I'm interested in learning Japanese.
examples.id: Saya tertarik belajar bahasa Jepang.

examples.en: Rina is good at cooking.
examples.id: Rina pintar memasak.

examples.en: Always check your ticket before leaving the station.
examples.id: Selalu cek tiketmu sebelum meninggalkan stasiun.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Dimas has a great camera and loves photography.

question.prompt: Complete: Dimas is very good at ___ photos.
question.explanation: **at** is a preposition, and after a preposition the verb takes **-ing**: good at **taking** photos. `at take` and `at to take` are wrong.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Which sentence uses the activity as the subject correctly?

options: Getting up early is hard for me.
Get up early is hard for me.
Getting up early are hard for me.
question.explanation: An activity as the subject takes **-ing**: **Getting up** early ... and the verb after it is singular: **is**. `Get up early is` uses the plain verb (the Indonesian pattern), and `are` is plural.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here is the whole lesson on one page. Learn the two lists.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · Gerunds & infinitives

Saya menghindari menyetir saat jam sibuk.
I miss eating my mother's rendang.

After a preposition (in, at, of, for, before, instead of): -ing, never the base form: interested **in learning**.
stop, remember and try change meaning with -ing or to (*stop smoking* = berhenti merokok; *stop to buy* = berhenti untuk membeli). You'll learn them later.

steps.text: Want more practice? These two British Council pages explain -ing forms and to-infinitives, with exercises.

id.greeting: Halo! Hari ini kamu akan menambah kata kerja di daftar -ing dan daftar to, dan belajar memakai -ing sebagai subjek dan setelah kata seperti in dan at. Yuk, pelan-pelan saja.

steps.title: Kata kerja + -ing lainnya
steps.text: Kamu sudah tahu I want to go dan I enjoy swimming. Sekarang kita tambah daftar -ing.
steps.body: Ulang sebentar: **want, need, hope + to** (I want **to go**); **enjoy, finish, don't mind + -ing** (I enjoy **swimming**). Delapan kata kerja lagi memakai **-ing**: **avoid, suggest, consider, keep, mind, practise, miss, can't stand**. Tidak ada aturan yang kelihatan: hafalkan setiap kata kerja bersama pasangannya, seperti kosakata baru. Jebakan: *menyarankan **untuk** pergi* membuat orang bilang `suggested to go`, padahal suggest memakai -ing: She suggested **going** by train.

steps.title: Kata kerja -ing dalam kehidupan nyata
steps.text: Perhatikan -ing setelah setiap kata kerja.
steps.body: **practise** adalah ejaan Inggris (British); bahasa Inggris Amerika menulis **practice** juga untuk kata kerja. **mind** kebanyakan dipakai dalam pertanyaan dan kalimat negatif: *Would you mind waiting?* / *I don't mind walking.*

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Rekan kerjamu bertanya cara ke Bandung. Apa saranmu?

question.prompt: Lengkapi: I suggest ___ the train. It's faster than the bus.
question.explanation: suggest diikuti **-ing**: I suggest **taking** the train. `suggest to take` datang dari *menyarankan untuk*, dan `suggest take` tidak memakai -ing.

steps.title: Kata kerja + to lainnya
steps.text: Sekarang daftar yang lain: kata kerja yang memakai to + bentuk dasar.
steps.body: Seperti *want* dan *hope*, kata kerja ini memakai **to + bentuk dasar** (kata kerja polos: *go, buy*): **decide, plan, afford, agree, refuse, promise, manage, offer, expect**. **afford** (mampu membayar) hampir selalu dipakai dengan **can / can't**: We can't afford **to buy** a car, bukan `can't afford buying`. **manage to** = *berhasil* (sulit, tapi kamu bisa), bukan *mengatur*. **offer to** = *menawarkan diri*.

steps.title: Kata kerja to dalam kehidupan nyata
steps.text: Ini contohnya dalam kalimat. Cari to + bentuk dasar.

steps.title: Susun kalimat
steps.text: Harga sewa mahal. Bilang bahwa uangmu tidak cukup untuk rumah besar.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Kami tidak mampu menyewa rumah besar.
question.solution: We can't afford to rent a big house.
question.explanation: **afford** memakai **to + bentuk dasar**: can't afford **to rent**. *tidak mampu* = can't afford; *menyewa* = rent.

steps.title: -ing sebagai subjek dan setelah preposisi
steps.text: Bagian terakhir: dua tempat lagi di mana bahasa Inggris perlu -ing.
steps.body: **1. Sebagai subjek** (hal yang dibicarakan kalimat): **Swimming** is good for you. *Berenang baik untuk kesehatan* memakai kata kerja polos, jadi orang menulis `Swim is good`. Kata kerja setelahnya tunggal: Swimming **is**. **2. Setelah preposisi**, kata penghubung kecil seperti *in, at, of, for, before, after, without, instead of*: pakai kata benda atau **-ing**, tidak pernah bentuk dasar: interested **in learning**, bukan `interested in learn`.

steps.title: -ing di tempat kerja
steps.text: Ini contoh subjek -ing dan -ing setelah preposisi.
steps.body: Frasa yang perlu diingat: **I look forward to meeting you.** Di sini *to* adalah preposisi (seperti *to the bank*), jadi setelahnya -ing.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Kalimat mana yang memakai kegiatan sebagai subjek dengan benar?

options: Getting up early is hard for me.
Get up early is hard for me.
Getting up early are hard for me.
question.explanation: Kegiatan sebagai subjek memakai **-ing**: **Getting up** early ... dan kata kerja setelahnya tunggal: **is**. `Get up early is` memakai kata kerja polos (pola bahasa Indonesia), dan `are` itu jamak.
